songdo_cloud_trails.description:
**Songdo Cloud Trails (송도구름산책로)** is a 365-metre curved skywalk that runs out over the sea from the eastern end of Songdo Beach. Opened in **2016**, it replaced the older Songdo Skywalk with a longer, gently serpentine deck ending in a small island viewing platform, and it is **free and open around the clock**.

The beach it starts from is **Korea's first modern public beach**, opened in **1913** — an 800 m by 50 m crescent of fine sand on Busan's southwest coast in Seo-gu. Sections of the walkway have glass floor panels, so you can watch the water move directly beneath you.
highlights: **365 m curved skywalk over the sea**, opened 2016 — replaced the older Songdo Skywalk
Glass floor panels along part of the deck; ends at a small island viewing platform
**Free, open 24 hours** — no ticket, no queue
Starts from **Korea's first modern public beach** (opened **1913**), 800 m x 50 m of fine sand
The Songdo Yonggung Suspension Bridge and the Amnam Park coastal trail continue from the western end
timeUsed: Drop-off at Songdo Marine Park and walk to the skywalk entrance (~4 min)
Out along the 365 m deck to the island platform and back (~12 min)
songdo_cloud_trails.whyOnRoute: After the dense Nampo-dong cluster and Gamcheon's hillside stairs, Songdo is the day's coastal reset. The Cloud Trails deck is **free, flat and about twenty minutes end to end**, which makes it the one Songdo experience every guest can do inside the stop window — whether or not they go on to take the cable car.

smartNotes.tip: The deck is exposed, so it can be windy and closes in severe weather — the guide swaps in the beach promenade when that happens.
smartNotes.photo: The curved deck sweeping over breaking waves; the glass floor panels looking straight down; the cable-car pylons rising behind the beach.
smartNotes.facilities: Public restrooms at Songdo Marine Park visitor centre; convenience stores along Songdohaebyeon-ro.

convenience.restroom: Songdo Marine Park visitor centre and convenience stores along Songdohaebyeon-ro

visitBasics.closed: Closed in high wind or severe weather

songdo_sky_park.description:
**Songdo Sky Park** sits on the Amnam Park headland at the far end of the **Songdo Marine Cable Car (Busan Air Cruise)** — a **1.62 km** round-trip line that crosses the bay at up to **86 m** above the water. The line first ran in 1964, closed in 1988, and **reopened in June 2017**.

The park at the top has sea-view decks looking back across the bay to Songdo Beach, landscaped walks, and a dinosaur-themed section that children tend to make straight for. From the decks the coastal trail continues down into Amnam Park proper.

**The cable car is not included in this tour.** It is an on-site choice paid at the station: **₩17,000 adult round-trip**, or **₩25,000** for the glass-floored Crystal cabin. Guests who would rather stay at sea level spend the stop on the beach promenade instead — the vehicle waits either way.
highlights: **Songdo Marine Cable Car (Busan Air Cruise)** — 1.62 km round trip, up to **86 m** above the bay
**Crystal cabin** option has a glass floor
Sea-view decks on the Amnam Park headland looking back across the bay
Dinosaur-themed park section; coastal trail continues into Amnam Park
**Cable car is an on-site paid choice — ₩17,000 adult round-trip, ₩25,000 Crystal cabin**
timeUsed: Ticket queue at the Songdo base station (~5 min)
Cable car crossing to the Amnam Park station (~7 min each way)
songdo_sky_park.whyOnRoute: This is the one stop on the day where the experience is the guest's to choose. Sky Park sits across the bay and the cable car is the way up to it, so the stop window is sized for the round trip. Guests who skip the ride are not left waiting anywhere awkward — the base station is on the beach the group has just walked.

smartNotes.tip: Buy at the base station; the Crystal cabin queue is usually longer than the standard one. If your ship's all-aboard is early, ride first and photograph from the top rather than lingering at the base.
smartNotes.photo: The bay from mid-crossing; the Sky Park decks looking back at Songdo Beach; the Crystal cabin's glass floor over open water.
smartNotes.facilities: Cafe and Korean War memorial exhibit at the lower station; restrooms at both stations.

convenience.parking: Songdo Marine Park public lot (base station)

visitBasics.hours: Cable car 09:00-21:00 (seasonal); Amnam Park headland open daily
visitBasics.closed: Cable car suspended in high wind or severe weather
visitBasics.walking: Easy — station lifts and level decks
visitBasics.admission: Cable car not included — ₩17,000 adult round-trip, ₩25,000 Crystal cabin, paid on site. Amnam Park itself is free.

pickupDescription:
Pickup is in the **arrival hall of whichever Busan cruise terminal your ship berths at** — the Busan International Cruise Terminal (Yeongdo) or the Busan Port International Passenger Terminal (Choryang). Neither is a default: it depends on where your ship docks, and it is confirmed at booking.

After disembarking, follow the signs to the arrival hall. Your guide is waiting there with an AtoC Korea sign and a printed itinerary card. Please be at the meeting point **by 08:50 for a 09:00 departure**.

The day runs about **8 hours**, ending back at your terminal around 17:00. The guide reconfirms your ship's all-aboard time at pickup and adjusts the running order if your sail-away is unusually early.
returnDescription:
The vehicle leaves the Yongdusan / Gwangbok-ro pickup point at about **16:45** and drives back through central Busan to **the same terminal you were collected from**, arriving at roughly **17:00** — about **8 hours** after pickup.

That leaves a comfortable buffer before the all-aboard times most Busan cruise calls use. If your ship sails unusually early, tell the guide at morning pickup: the running order is adjusted on the day, usually by trimming the Songdo and Yongdusan stops.

routeShapeIntro.subtitle: Cruise terminal pickup at 09:00; northeast to Haedong Yonggungsa first, while the cliff is still quiet; back across the city for the UN Memorial Cemetery and lunch at your own expense; then Nampo-dong walked end to end as three separate stops (Jagalchi, BIFF Square, Gukje Market); Gamcheon's painted hillside; Songdo for the Cloud Trails skywalk and, if you take the cable car, Sky Park across the bay; Yongdusan Park last, and back at your terminal by 17:00.

routePhases.description: Cruise terminal pickup at 09:00 with a disembarkation buffer, then northeast along the coast to Haedong Yonggungsa for a 09:45 arrival — ahead of the tour-bus surge that builds from mid-morning.
UN Memorial Cemetery (30 min) for Korean War context, then a Busan-specific lunch — dwaeji-gukbap or milmyeon — at your own expense.
Jagalchi Market, BIFF Square and Gukje Market are three separate stops within about 600 m of each other, so the middle of the day is walked rather than driven.
Gamcheon Culture Village (45 min) for the painted-house panorama, reached by a short transfer from Nampo-dong.
Songdo Cloud Trails skywalk, then Sky Park across the bay if you choose the cable car, and Yongdusan Park before the drive back — at the terminal by 17:00, and always timed to your ship's all-aboard.

stopWhyOnRoute.pickup: Picking you up in the terminal arrival hall removes the one thing that goes wrong on a port day: finding local transport with a clock running. The 09:00 meet leaves clear time after the ship's morning disembarkation and still fits the full nine-stop route into an eight-hour day, back at the terminal by 17:00.
stopWhyOnRoute.jagalchi: Busan's identity is built on seafood the way Seoul's is built on royal Joseon palace cuisine, and Jagalchi is the single most essential expression of it. It also sits at the entrance to the Nampo-dong cluster, which is why the middle of the day pivots here: Jagalchi, BIFF Square and Gukje Market are three separate stops inside a 600 m walking radius, done on foot rather than by road.
stopWhyOnRoute.gamcheon: The route's most colourful stop — there is no other neighbourhood like it in Korea. The Korean War thread runs straight through it: the UN Memorial Cemetery is the memorial, Gamcheon is the lived consequence, a refugee settlement that became a community. Forty-five minutes is enough for the main photo loop from the observation deck down through the painted lanes.
stopWhyOnRoute.yongdusan: Yongdusan gives you Busan's most recognised 360-degree panorama and closes the loop on foot: the park sits directly above the Nampo-dong streets the group walked earlier, so the last stop reframes the day from above before the short drive back to the ship.
stopWhyOnRoute.return: The cruise-terminal return is the day's hard constraint. Dropping off at about 17:00 — eight hours after pickup — leaves a real buffer before the all-aboard times most Busan port calls use, and the guide adjusts the running order on the day if your ship sails unusually early.

gamcheonTip: Residents live here — keep voices down, no drones, take your rubbish with you; wear grippy shoes for the steep lanes. The village is at its quietest in the early afternoon, after the morning tour groups have moved on.

routeLogic.returnGuarantee: The route is built around a 17:00 return to the terminal you were collected from — eight hours after a 09:00 pickup, which leaves a comfortable buffer before the all-aboard times most Busan port calls use. If your ship sails unusually early, the guide adjusts the running order on the day.
routeLogic.directPickup: No subway transfers, no city-hotel transfers — you are collected at the cruise terminal arrival hall at 09:00 and dropped back at the same point at about 17:00. Which of the two Busan cruise terminals applies to you depends on where your ship berths, and is confirmed at booking.
routeLogic.gamcheonTiming: Gamcheon gets 45 minutes in the early afternoon, once the morning tour groups have cleared the observation deck. Placing it after the Nampo-dong markets means the walk runs downhill through the painted lanes rather than up them.
routeLogic.yongdusanTiming: Yongdusan is the day's closing stop because it sits directly above the Nampo-dong streets you walked earlier — the last twenty minutes reframe the whole afternoon from above, and the terminal is a short drive from the same pickup point.
routeLogic.cableCarTradeoff: Songdo Marine Cable Car (₩17,000 adult round-trip) and the Busan Diamond Tower observatory (₩12,000) are not in the tour price. The cable car is an on-site choice at the Songdo stop: ride it up to Sky Park, or stay at sea level and walk the free Cloud Trails skywalk instead.
routeLogic.fixedWindows: The 20–50 minute stop windows are fixed across the group. You can choose what to do inside a stop — ride the Songdo cable car up to Sky Park or walk the free skywalk instead, go up the Busan Diamond Tower or stay at park level — but you cannot lengthen a stop or drop one. Guests who want the day reshaped around them should take the private charter.

cableCarFaq.question: Can I ride the Songdo Marine Cable Car?
cableCarFaq.answer: Yes — it is the Songdo Sky Park stop, and it is your choice on the day. The cable car is not included in the tour price: you buy at the base station, ₩17,000 adult round-trip or ₩25,000 for the glass-floored Crystal cabin. If you would rather not ride, spend the stop on the free Cloud Trails skywalk and the beach promenade instead; the vehicle waits either way.

lunchHighlights: Lunch is at your own expense — it is not included in the tour price
**Dwaeji-gukbap** (Busan pork-bone soup) or **milmyeon** (Busan cold wheat noodles) — both regional specialities
Both dishes have Korean War refugee origins unique to Busan
Typical price ₩8,000–12,000 per dish; drinks ₩3,000–6,000 if ordered
Vegetarian / halal-friendly substitution available on request at booking

tierComparisonFaq.question: How is the bus tour different from the small-group cruise tour?
tierComparisonFaq.answer: Same nine stops, same 8-hour day, different vehicle. This tour runs on a large coach shared with cruise passengers from several ships, at US$58.79 per person. The small-group tour runs the identical route in a van capped at 12 guests, at US$68.95 per person. Choose the coach on price; choose the van for a quieter group and a little more flexibility in how long each stop actually runs.
